status: John approved the simplified Bottles over canes illustration on 19 November 2026.

approval.scope: The two-stage Bottles over canes illustration

brief: Make the bottle method easy to read at its printed size. Show one intact bottle, mouth down around the cane with its closed base at the top, beside a small group of plants sheltered by fleece resting on four such supports.
source: John’s Best Garden Fleece Support, 11 April 2026. The film shows a longer bed using more bottles. The book picture is a simplified reconstruction of the method.

references: Both camera crops in the order above on a single canvas, separated by a 28 px white gutter
generation.prompt:
Redraw the first reference as TWO crisp, simple documentary gardening photographs for a small UK book illustration. Show exactly how an ordinary upturned green bottle on a vertical bamboo cane supports horticultural fleece above a vegetable crop. The first reference is a two-picture layout made from the gardener’s actual 11 April allotment footage. Keep its two-panel structure, aspect and approximate camera directions; simplify and move in on the gardening job. The 2nd reference is the previous published pair, ONLY for bottle type, planting method and location. Avoid its several confusing overlapping structures. Plain natural daylight and true textures, colour and scale consistent across the pair. No writing, arrows or labels, no people, no diagrams. Deliver a broad horizontal photographic diptych in approximately 2.55:1 proportion. Left panel has about one third of the full width, right panel about two thirds, separated by a perfectly straight narrow plain white vertical gutter. Full bleed top and bottom.
LEFT picture is one exceptionally clear bottle-over-cane detail, photographed slightly from the side, with the entire bottle, exposed support shaft and its contact with dark soil visible. Just ONE ordinary intact slender green translucent glass beer bottle, label removed, OPEN small threaded or lipped glass neck pointing DOWN with a distinct open rim snug over the single upright tan bamboo garden cane. WIDE closed rounded bottle base pointing UP. Slender single straight bamboo shaft rises from the soil for about 12–15 cm before entering the open neck and continuing INSIDE the bottle to its closed broad base. Its pale shaft is faintly visible THROUGH translucent green glass. The bottle is lifted clear of the ground so the exposed cane is obvious. No cap, no cap on the cane, no fence, no fabric, no other bottle or stakes. A single tiny seedling offset to the side can give scale. Quiet background of cultivated soil, realistic but softened. Bottle and cane centred so the whole assembly reads immediately even as a thumbnail. Leave modest breathing room above the bottle and below the soil contact.
RIGHT picture is a straightforward modest individual bed in the same green Cornish allotment, seen from a low oblique angle looking down slightly, close enough to read the technique. A small roughly rectangular group of FOUR short independent upright slender bamboo canes in soil around just THREE or FOUR individually spaced, different-sized vegetable seedlings. Each cane has one upturned GREEN glass bottle seated over its top, just like the detail on the left. Gently lay ONE continuous light semi-translucent white nonwoven horticultural fleece over the FOUR CLOSED UPPERMOST BOTTLE BASES so that the smooth glass bears the fabric clear of the plants. Show a shallow broad canopy that bridges the four corner bottles; slight natural sag in the middle with a clear air gap over the leaves. Sides fall down towards soil and the hem is held by two or three ordinary small bricks or stones. The fleece should be thin and evenly lit enough that a reader can distinguish especially BOTH NEAR green bottle silhouettes and the cane below them THROUGH the near face, together with the foliage at lower level. A green silhouette must not protrude through the unbroken white surface. The upper supports read as smooth rounded shoulders, not sharp poles. No joining bamboo or horizontal rails, no arches, no strings, no commercial frame, no tennis balls, no spare bottles. Simple, recognisable dark allotment soil and the edge of a short brick path and strip of clear grass at the margin from the source. Closely framed ground-level scene; keep the surrounding tarps, bins, sheds and neighbouring crops outside the crop. All four corners of this little covered bed and ground anchors fit comfortably within the right panel. Make visually obvious in one glance what touches the fleece and where it is held above the crop.

layout.change: The bare support needs less width. Both images retain the original outer boundaries, height and 4.6 pt gutter. The wider photograph shows all four corners.
